extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and advanced students (readers of a 19th‑century mathematical journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Derive equations and prove properties of conic sections, hyperboloids, plane quadrilaterals, and related centres/ loci; includes worked solutions and methods (analytic geometry, coordinates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of equation for hyperboloids whose asymptotic cones touch three given planes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperboloids with the origin for centre have equations of the form A x^2 + B y^2 + C z^2 + 2D yz + 2E zx + 2F xy = ±1, and their asymptotic cones have the homogeneous form A x^2 + B y^2 + C z^2 + 2D yz + 2E zx + 2F xy = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the asymptotic cone touches the three coordinate planes, the traces on those planes must be perfect squares, implying D = −BC, E = −AC, F = ±AB. Rejecting the sign that makes the cone a complete square yields the general cone equation A x^2 + B y^2 + C z^2 − 2BC y z − 2AC x z − 2AB x y = 0, and the corresponding hyperboloid equation A x^2 + B y^2 + C z^2 − 2BC y z − 2AC x z − 2AB x y = ±1. The choice of ± determines one‑ or two‑sheeted hyperboloids; A, B, C are arbitrary (sign conventions noted). Substituting change‑of‑coordinate relations when the given planes are not coordinate planes yields an equivalent form (5').

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that traces on coordinate planes be complete squares when cone touches those planes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a cone whose surface is tangent to a coordinate plane, the quadratic form restricted to that plane must be a perfect square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From this condition one deduces linear relations among cross coefficients (e.g., D = −BC, E = −AC, F = ±AB). The sign choices are subject to overall sign conventions of A, B, C; one sign may produce a complete square for the whole cone and is to be rejected in the construction of distinct asymptotic cones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of conics through four points by position of a point
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of four points is without the triangle formed by the other three, there can pass through the points an indefinite number of ellipses, an indefinite number of hyperbolas, and two parabolas; if the point is within that triangle, only hyperbolas pass through the given points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification follows from the signs of parameters in the general second‑order equation through the four points; the geometric location of the fourth point relative to the triangle formed by the other three determines the admissible types of conics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chord of contact property for circumscribed conics (points E and F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a series of conic sections circumscribed to a given quadrilateral ABCD with diagonals intersecting at O and opposite sides meeting in E and F, all points of contact corresponding to E lie on the line OF, and those corresponding to F lie on OE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by equating the chord‑of‑contact expression to the chord through the corresponding vertex; coordinates of E and F satisfy the chord equations, hence the locus of contact points is a fixed line through O.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common intersection of diagonals of circumscribed quadrilaterals
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagonals of all circumscribed quadrilaterals (to the same family of second‑order curves through A,B,C,D) pass through the same point — the intersection O of the diagonals of the inscribed quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown by combining tangent equations so that absolute terms vanish, giving lines through the origin (chosen as O); holds for any value of the arbitrary parameter in the family of conics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersections of opposite sides of circumscribed figures lie on EF
rubrics_metrics.description: The points of intersection of the opposite sides of the circumscribed figures lie on the fixed line EF determined by the original quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine equations of pairs of opposite sides; resulting equations identical with the equation of EF (22), hence all such intersection points lie on EF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonic division on each of the six lines of the complete quadrilateral
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the six lines determined by joining the four given points in pairs, there are four points of intersection at which the line is harmonically divided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general property: chords, tangents and points of contact yield harmonic quadruples when derived from intersections and chord‑of‑contact relations with respect to conics passing through the four points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus of centres of all conics through four given points (equation (25))
rubrics_metrics.description: The locus of centres of all conic sections passing through four given points A,B,C,D is given by a specific second‑degree equation (25); its type (hyperbola or ellipse) depends on the relative position of the points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one of the four points is outside the triangle formed by the other three the locus is a hyperbola; if inside, the locus is an ellipse. The equation (25) is derived by eliminating the arbitrary parameter b from the partial derivative conditions of the general conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelism of conjugate diameters and sides/diagonals (properties of locus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The coefficients of the locus equation make the axes (or diagonals AC, BD) parallel to conjugate diameters; the locus has three pairs of conjugate diameters parallel, respectively, to AB & CD, BC & AD, AC & BD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the vanishing of the xy coefficient and symmetry: choosing different axes (e.g., EC, ED) yields a similarly formed locus; geometric interpretation ties conjugate diameters to sides of quadrilateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle points, intersections, and centre of the locus (property m)
rubrics_metrics.description: The middle points of opposite sides, the intersections of opposite sides, and the middle points of diagonals all satisfy the locus equation; the three straight lines joining middle points of opposite sides and both diagonals intersect in the centre of the locus of centres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinates of these special points explicitly satisfy equation (25); algebraic elimination yields the common intersection equal to the centre of (25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Four circles through triangles formed by producing opposite sides intersect in a common point (theorem n)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pairs of opposite sides AB, CD and AD, BC of ABCD are produced to meet and a circle is described about each of the four triangles so formed, the four circles intersect in the same point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the conics in (34)–(37) are circles (coefficients satisfy circle conditions), the algebra shows these circles share a common intersection P; additional properties include the centres of these circles lying on another circle through P and perpendiculars from P to the sides lying on one line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further circle relations (o, p, q)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the four circles described about the four triangles meet in P: (o) the centres of the four circles lie on another circle passing through P; (p) perpendiculars from P to the sides AB, BC, CD, DA meet the sides in four collinear points; (q) for cyclic A,B,C,D the difference of squares of the radii of the first two circles equals that of the other two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are corollaries following from the circle constructions and algebraic conditions on coefficients; proofs are sketched or left as exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for finding the centre of gravity Q of a quadrilateral (r,s,t,u)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several constructive methods to find the centroid Q of quadrilateral ABCD (diagonals meeting at O): (r) use triangle centroids and parallels (draw EG, FH parallel to BD, AC); (s) set off one‑third differences on segments and complete a parallelogram; (t) from centroid of triangle A,B,O draw EG parallel to BD and make EQ = one third of OD; (u) bisect opposite sides to meet at P, then extend OP to Q with PQ = (1/3)OP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each method yields the same centroid coordinates x = 1/3(a−c), y = 1/3(b−d) when using diagonals AC, BD as axes and coordinates as given. Method (s) is historical (Mechanic's Magazine, Lady's Diary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of quadrilateral formed by triangle centroids E,F,G,H
rubrics_metrics.description: Joining the centres of gravity of the four triangles composed two and two of the quadrilateral produces another quadrilateral EFGH similar to ABCD but reversed in position; its area equals one ninth of the original, its diagonals intersect at the original centroid Q and are parallel to and one third the length of the original diagonals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinates and length relations are given explicitly: EG = 1/3 BD, FH = 1/3 AC, and E,G etc. lie on lines parallel to diagonals; proofs by coordinate expressions (43–46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelogram of centres of gravity of diagonal triangles (KLMN) and its properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The centres of gravity of the four triangles formed by the two diagonals (with common vertex O) form a parallelogram KLMN whose sides are parallel to the quadrilateral's diagonals and equal to EG, FH. Its diagonals intersect on the line OQ (line through centroid and intersection of diagonals). The area of this parallelogram is two ninths of the quadrilateral's area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinates of K,L,M,N given explicitly; relations to E,F,G,H and to O,Q are detailed with equations (62)–(68). The construction can be iterated to form a series of parallelograms and inscribed quadrilaterals with areas following the geometric series noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series construction of nested parallelograms/quadrilaterals via centres of gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterating the process of taking centres of gravity of triangles formed by diagonals produces a sequence of parallelograms and inscribed quadrilaterals whose areas form the series A/9, A/81, A/729, ... with A the area of the original quadrilateral; all diagonals intersect on the line OQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area scaling factors and concurrency of diagonals on OQ are given; the construction and algebraic verification are sketched and left for further investigation.
